article.headline: One Penalty, One Position: Why George Russell's COTA Incident Sent Antonelli's Title to Mexico

research.facts:
Russell Penalty — Why Antonelli Didn't Clinch at COTA
**Verified Facts (MEDIUM-HIGH):**
- George Russell received a 5-second penalty at COTA for a Lap 1 incident
- Penalty dropped Russell from P7 to P8 in final classification
- For Antonelli to clinch at COTA, Russell needed to finish outside the top 10
- Because Russell finished P8 (not outside top 10), Antonelli's title moves to Mexico City
- Antonelli still needs only P9 or better in Mexico City to clinch
**Confidence:** MEDIUM-HIGH (FIA report and Silverstone title permutations article confirmed the penalty angle; GPFans confirmed the math)

Mexico City GP Strategy / Altitude Preview
**Verified Facts (HIGH — established F1 technical facts):**
- Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez altitude: 2,240 metres above sea level
- Altitude effects: reduced air density affects power unit (less oxygen for combustion), aerodynamic downforce, and cooling
- Lap count: 71 laps, circuit length 4.304 km
- Race Sunday: November 1, 2026, 14:00 local (20:00 CET)
- No sprint race format at Mexico City 2026
- Tyre behaviour at altitude differs from sea-level circuits — degradation patterns can be non-linear
**Confidence:** HIGH (Formula1.com Mexico GP page and Crash.net calendar confirmed schedule/lap data)
